title: First cohomology lifts a supported quotient section to an affine nonvanishing locus
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq X$ an affine open, $x\in U$, and $\mathcal M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] with free generator $a$ on $U$. Let $\mathcal I$ be the reduced vanishing ideal of the closed subset $X\setminus U$, namely $\mathcal I(V)=\{b\in\mathcal O_X(V):b(z)=0\text{ in }\kappa(z)\text{ for all }z\in V\setminus U\}$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Let $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal I$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [pqf-def-coherent] with $\mathcal J_x=\mathfrak m_x\subseteq\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. In the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], put $\mathcal Q=\mathcal I/\mathcal J$. Suppose the canonical tensor sequence [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M\longrightarrow\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal M\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal M\longrightarrow0$$
is short exact and the canonical multiplication map $\iota:\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal M\to\mathcal M$, induced by $\mathcal I\hookrightarrow\mathcal O_X$ and locally given by $b\otimes m\mapsto bm$, is injective. Let $q\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal M)$ have nonzero germ under the canonical quotient identification $(\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal M)_x\cong\mathcal M_x/\mathfrak m_x\mathcal M_x$ induced by $\iota$. If $H^1(X,\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M)=0$ [pqf-def-cohomology], there exists $t\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal M)$ with $\pi(t)=q$. For $s=\iota(t)\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal M)$, the residue of $s$ at $x$ is nonzero and the residue of $s$ at every $z\in X\setminus U$ is zero. Writing $s|_U=f a$ for $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, its nonvanishing locus $X_s=\{y:s_y\notin\mathfrak m_y\mathcal M_y\}$ [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] satisfies $x\in X_s=U_f\subseteq U$, where $U_f=\{y\in U:f_y\text{ is a unit in }\mathcal O_{X,y}\}$. In particular $X_s$ is affine.

proof.text: The module-sheaf category is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], and $\Gamma(X,-)$ is additive and left exact by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] to the assumed short exact tensor sequence. With the natural identification $R^0\Gamma=\Gamma$ and cohomology as in [pqf-def-cohomology], its exact segment is $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I\otimes\mathcal M)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(\pi)}\Gamma(X,\mathcal Q\otimes\mathcal M)\xrightarrow{\delta}H^1(X,\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal M)$. Naturality of $R^0\Gamma\cong\Gamma$ identifies its first arrow with the actual section map of $\pi$.

source.place: Tag 015B, lemma-higher-derived-functors, parts (2) and (4), applied to the tensor sequence in Tag 0B5P.

proof.text: The last group in Step 1 is zero by hypothesis, so $\delta(q)=0$. Exactness gives $t$ with $\pi(t)=q$. Put $s=\iota(t)$. Taking the germ of this equality at $x$ and applying the quotient identification assumed in the statement sends $q_x$ to the class of $s_x$ in $\mathcal M_x/\mathfrak m_x\mathcal M_x$. This class is nonzero by the hypothesis on $q$. Thus $x\in X_s$.

proof.text: For $z\in X\setminus U$, every $b\in\mathcal I_z$ is represented on some neighbourhood $V$ of $z$ by a section of $\mathcal I(V)$, by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. The defining vanishing condition for $\mathcal I(V)$ says that its image in $\kappa(z)=\mathcal O_{X,z}/\mathfrak m_z$ is zero [def-weil-residue-field]. Hence $\mathcal I_z\subseteq\mathfrak m_z$.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-invertible, proof, first paragraph: lifting the quotient section and identifying its affine nonvanishing open.

proof.text: Use the canonical tensor-stalk isomorphism [lem-pc-ringed-space-module-stalk-tensor] at $z\notin U$. Write the image of $t_z$ as a finite sum $\sum_i b_i\otimes m_i$, with $b_i\in\mathcal I_z$ and $m_i\in\mathcal M_z$. The stalk of the canonical multiplication map sends this to $s_z=\sum_i b_i m_i$. Step 3 puts every $b_i$ in $\mathfrak m_z$, so $s_z\in\mathfrak m_z\mathcal M_z$. Its residue is zero. This proves $X_s\subseteq U$.

source.place: Tag 01CB, lemma-stalk-tensor-product, applied to the multiplication map in Tag 0B5P.

proof.text: Because $a$ is a free generator on $U$, there is a unique $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ with $s|_U=fa$. For $y\in U$ the basis $a_y$ identifies $\mathcal M_y/\mathfrak m_y\mathcal M_y$ with $\mathcal O_{X,y}/\mathfrak m_y$ and sends the class of $s_y$ to that of $f_y$. This class is nonzero exactly when $f_y\notin\mathfrak m_y$, equivalently when $f_y$ is a unit in the local ring. Consequently $X_s\cap U=U_f$; together with Steps 2 and 4 this gives $x\in X_s=U_f\subseteq U$.

source.place: Tag 0B5P, lemma-quasi-compact-h1-zero-invertible, proof, first paragraph: lifting the quotient section and identifying its affine nonvanishing open.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime] to the given affine open $U$ and $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$. Its affine open $D(f)$ is the residue-nonzero locus of $f$, which is exactly $U_f$ by Step 5. Therefore $X_s=U_f=D(f)$ is affine.
